package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to any project using committed vendor directories)
package_info.why_malicious: Malicious code can be injected into vendored dependencies within Go projects because the Go toolchain's integrity checks (go mod verify, GOSUMDB) do not apply to files in the vendor directory. This allows attackers to introduce arbitrary code that will be built and executed as part of the application, bypassing standard module verification mechanisms.

execution_context.trigger: build-time and runtime (when the application is built and executed)
execution_context.file_location: vendor/<dependency>/malicious.go (or any file within the vendor directory)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code reads the SECRET_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value to a remote attacker-controlled server via HTTP POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Vendored dependencies are not expected to contain code that exfiltrates environment variables or communicates with external servers. Such behavior is a hallmark of supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal vendored code should match the upstream open-source dependency and not contain unauthorized changes or side effects. Malicious code in vendor directories violates this expectation by introducing hidden, potentially harmful logic.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate dependencies may perform network requests as part of their documented functionality, but not for exfiltrating environment variables or secrets without user knowledge.
key_indicators: Unexpected network requests in vendored code
init() functions with side effects in dependencies
Code present in vendor directory but not in upstream source

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious code into a vendored dependency file (e.g., vendor/somepkg/malicious.go) before code review or after initial dependency commit.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the build and executed when the application starts or imports the affected package.

attack_chain.action: During application build or runtime, the malicious code executes, harvesting secrets from environment variables and exfiltrating them to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive credentials or secrets from the victim environment.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests originating from vendored dependency code
Vendored files containing init() functions with side effects
Vendored code accessing environment variables or sensitive files
file_indicators: vendor/<dependency>/*.go files with code not matching upstream source
Unexpected new or modified files in vendor directory
init() functions or network code in vendor directory
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to unknown or attacker-controlled domains from build or runtime processes
Connections initiated by the application at startup to external IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Regularly compare vendored dependency files against their upstream sources to detect unauthorized changes. Monitor for unexpected network activity originating from the application, especially during build or startup. Use scripts (like Kubernetes' verify-vendor.sh) to validate the integrity of the vendor directory. Flag any vendored code that accesses environment variables or performs network operations not present in the official dependency.
